column1: # Argument and result signatures of the game's Lua natives (game_lua_api.tsv), derived statically from the
# TU1 binary (Fable2TU1 default.xex) in IDA. Nothing here was observed at runtime.
# How: each native is registered through a binder that pushes a C closure (lua_pushcclosure 0x8219AA80); the
# closure is the typed glue that reads the Lua stack and calls the native. Its reads give the arguments, the
# constant it leaves in r3 at each return gives the result count, its stack pushes give the result types.
# Natives whose closure only forwards lua_State (plain lua_CFunction, or (object, lua_State*) methods) are
# Columns: table, name, address (TU1, as in game_lua_api.tsv), args, results, detail.
#   args: Lua stack positions 1..n, comma-separated. Types: number, integer (read as a number and truncated
#     to int), boolean, string, table, function, any (accepted without a type check, e.g. a value the native
#     keeps a reference to), entity (userdata resolved to an entity), userdata (unresolved userdata, incl.
#     light userdata such as FNVHash IDs), or a userdata class named by its metatable (CVector3, CRecordPtr,
#     CI32Vector2, C2DBoxI, CInventoryItemPtr, CScriptSearchHandle, CMessageEvent, CZoomer, CLookAtHandle,
#     CAnimationControlSimple, CAnimationControlBlend). "a|b" = the native accepts either (overloads).
#     "?" = a position the native skips or that could not be resolved. "t..." = further arguments of
#     type t read in a loop. Empty = the native reads no arguments. For *Metatable tables argument 1 is self.
#   results: count returned to Lua, then ":" and the pushed types in order when known; "0" = nothing;
#     "?" = the count differs between return paths (detail lists them) or could not be determined.
# Coverage: 3111 full, 27 partial (some positions "?"/any), 464 no arguments read, of 3602 natives.
